title: Siblings Discuss a Promise That Became Inconvenient
script: Sinta: [thoughtful] Rian, do you remember you promised to help me move my furniture this weekend? Something came up, and I need to know if you can still come.
Rian: Actually, my friends invited me on a trip that same weekend, and honestly, I would much rather go with them than carry boxes all day.
Sinta: [carefully] I understand wanting to have fun, but I already told the moving company not to send extra workers because you said you would help.
Rian: It's just furniture, Sinta. Can't you hire someone else, or ask a neighbor instead of relying only on me?
Sinta: [reflective] I could, but that is not really the point. You gave me your word, and now you want to change it because something better appeared.
Rian: When you put it that way, it does sound worse than I meant it to be.
Sinta: [honestly] A promise that only counts when it's convenient isn't really a promise at all; it's just an offer you can cancel whenever you feel like it.
Rian: I never thought about it like that. I suppose I have done this before, and you never said anything.
Sinta: [seriously] I have noticed, but I stayed quiet because I did not want to seem like I was keeping score between us.
Rian: Even though this trip sounds appealing, I would feel guilty the entire time knowing I let you down for something less important.
Sinta: [gently] I'm not trying to guilt you, Rian. I just want you to understand what it costs me when plans depend on your word and then change.
Rian: You're right, and I'll tell my friends I can't go this time. Helping you move matters more than one weekend trip.
Sinta: [encouraging] Thank you. It means more to me than the furniture itself, honestly, that you chose to keep your word despite the trip.
Rian: From now on, if I'm not sure I can keep a promise, I'll say so honestly instead of agreeing just to avoid an awkward conversation.
Sinta: [sincere] That would help both of us. Now, are you ready to lift something heavy this weekend?
Rian: As long as you make coffee first, yes, I'm ready.

quiz.question: What did Rian promise to help Sinta with?
quiz.explanation: Rian had promised to help Sinta move her furniture this weekend.

quiz.question: Why does Rian want to cancel the plan?
options: His friends invited him on a trip the same weekend
He forgot how to move furniture
quiz.explanation: Rian's friends invited him on a trip that same weekend, and he would rather go with them.

quiz.question: What had Sinta already done because Rian promised to help?
options: Told the moving company not to send extra workers
quiz.explanation: Sinta had already told the moving company not to send extra workers because Rian said he would help.

quiz.question: How does Sinta describe a promise that only counts when convenient?
options: Not really a promise at all, just a cancellable offer
quiz.explanation: Sinta says a promise that only counts when convenient isn't really a promise, just an offer that can be canceled.

quiz.question: What does Rian decide to do in the end?
options: Ask Sinta to postpone the move
Tell his friends he can't go and help Sinta move instead
quiz.explanation: Rian decides to tell his friends he can't go this time because helping Sinta move matters more.

quiz.question: Why is the promise important?
options: Sinta relied on it when arranging the move

quiz.question: What should Rian do if conflict appears early?
options: Notify Sinta promptly and help find an agreed alternative

quiz.question: What if he cannot safely lift furniture?
options: Say so and arrange suitable help rather than overpromise

quiz.question: What makes a promise different from a casual offer?
options: Another person may plan and incur costs in reliance on it

quiz.question: What does Rian change?
options: He will be honest about uncertainty before committing
